races.name: Van Buck 50th Anniversary Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)
#Come Racing Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator stepping up from 7f on consistent Good-ground form (4 of last 5 runs on similar going), but needs genuine pace to exploit; trainer Joseph Parr has no winners in the last 14 days (0/6) and the horse's last win at this trip is unproven.|

runners_data.name: Mertoun
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam in fair recent form (3/14 last 14 days) and Mertoun brings back-to-back mile wins on Good ground — the form profile here is the most immediately relevant in the field for this trip and surface combination.|

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and pace anchor for this race, though his last five runs show consistent placing without winning; Charlie Johnston's yard is active (5/34) and Jack Mitchell is a competent handler, but the horse's task is to control rather than overpower.|

runners_data.name: Venetian Lion
runners_data.note: William Haggas's runner wears headgear and has course-winning form over this exact mile trip; racing prominently suits the unfolding shape well, and the stable's 6/37 14-day strike rate flags genuine in-form confidence behind this runner.|

runners_data.name: Legacy Rock
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over this course and trip make Legacy Rock's profile directly relevant; the 51-day absence is a query but the headgear is retained and Dr Newland & Insole's runner has strong Good-ground figures across nine runs (2 wins, 3 places).|

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Benoit de la Sayette partners this four-year-old who is a genuine hold-up type by inclination; the map places him in midfield because the rear of the field is saturated with closers, and his STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) reflects that compromise — his best form also comes over 10f rather than a flat mile.|

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer takes over on this four-year-old who has shown only hold-up tendencies across recent starts, all on going similar to today's; pushed into a midfield map position because the true back of the field is full, his STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is genuine and Spencer will need a pace scenario that doesn't materialise easily from this shape.|

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who, with Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) aboard, has good in-running speed but the field's prominent roles are already occupied; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects his likely struggle to obtain his preferred position, and his recent form (9-7-3-0-4-3) shows inconsistency on soft and standard variants rather than pure Good to Firm.|

races.paceDynamic: Glen Nevis is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, he should slot onto the lead from his prominent draw and dictate a steady, controlled tempo over this Newmarket mile on Good to Firm ground. The field contains more pace than the map reflects — Calyxoh is a natural prominent type and both Potomac River and Big Alex Walmsley are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield because the rear is already crowded with true closers; Venetian Lion and Legacy Rock are also happy to race prominently, meaning Glen Nevis may face some early company despite being the standout pace horse. With Glen Nevis able to set a sustainable gallop uncontested or only lightly pressed, the race is likely to develop into a test of quality rather than stamina, with the tempo unlikely to be truly searching. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can travel into the race comfortably, as a moderate gallop into a fast finish will disadvantage deep closers who need a strong end-to-end tempo to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Glen Nevis Controls, Stays Honest
scenarios.trigger: If Glen Nevis leads at a fair but unhurried tempo and the race resolves into a quality-driven finish from the front two or three.
scenarios.body: Glen Nevis dictates from the front, with Venetian Lion and Legacy Rock tracking him into the straight before the race quickens from 2f out; horses that have been racing prominently and can sustain a late kick hold a clear edge. Mertoun's strong recent form over this course and distance makes him dangerous swooping from just off the pace, but the structural advantage lies with those who have saved energy by travelling close to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Lion, Legacy Rock and Glen Nevis race in a tight cluster throughout and the race becomes a battle of the front-runners from 2f home.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to sort them out on merit, and with the William Haggas yard in strong form (T14: 6/37), Venetian Lion is well placed to quicken off the gallop; Legacy Rock's back-to-back wins over this trip and surface give him solid claims in a truly-run prominent battle. Hold-up horses who cannot get to the action will be left waiting for a gap that arrives too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners press each other harder than expected and the pace is genuinely searching, opening the door for the hold-up runners to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Mertoun's consistent form at the mile on Good ground makes him the logical beneficiary if the tempo does lift; Wield has shown ability to finish powerfully from off a strong pace. However, this scenario is partially undermined by the fact that Potomac River and Big Alex Walmsley, though natural hold-up horses, have been mapped to midfield and face a compromised position, reducing the depth of late-running firepower.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches throughout due to the moderate pace and the race dissolves into a sprint finish where position and luck in running become decisive.
scenarios.body: A compressed, field-wide sprint from the 2f marker suits horses with a sharp turn of foot, and Venetian Lion's headgear and Calyxoh's prominent tendencies could both see them involved; however, Calyxoh is a redistributed prominent type racing out of its natural role and its STYLE_FIT discount applies here. This is the least predictable outcome and the least likely given a single clear pace-setter who should produce an orderly tempo.

watchPoints.text: Glen Nevis controls the tempo entirely uncontested — if he bowls along at a comfortable clip, every prominent horse behind him gets a free ride into the straight and the hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged from early.|

Calyxoh and Venetian Lion could both push forward early to claim prominent ground, creating a brief flurry of pace pressure on Glen Nevis in the first 2f — watch whether this settles quickly or forces a faster first half than the shape suggests.|

Potomac River and Big Alex Walmsley are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield by necessity; if Jamie Spencer or Benoit de la Sayette drop them in behind anyway, the closers' cluster could be unusually large and create traffic problems in the straight.|

Mertoun's form profile (two wins and a place in last three runs at the mile on Good ground) is the most directly transferable to today's conditions — monitor how Rob Hornby positions him early as a signal of confidence or concern from the yard.|

Legacy Rock's 51-day absence is the main unknown in an otherwise strong profile; watch for any market drift on course that would suggest connections have questions about his fitness returning from the layoff.|

races.name: National Stud Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Astro King
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old Daniel & Claire Kubler veteran who races out of the back and needs a strong pace to reel in leaders at 1m4f; his sim-going record of 11/15 with 2W3P is respectable but form of 90/005 suggests he is on a slide, and an uncontested leader makes his closing runs harder to land.|

runners_data.name: Tycoon
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's four-year-old has placed at 12f on good twice recently and maps comfortably to a prominent position just off the leader; 26 days since last run is no concern, and his 9/11 sim-going record underlines reliable consistency on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Race To The Stars
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's string is flying (T14: 13/27) and Race To The Stars won over 11f on standard Tapeta before a soft-ground fourth at 12f; the 266-day absence is the one question mark, though Appleby's squad tend to arrive ready, and good-to-firm suits his best form.|

runners_data.name: Round The Table
runners_data.note: Has won his last two starts at 10f on good ground and gets a dream opportunity to dictate an uncontested tempo on fast ground; the tongue tie is noted, but his three-from-three record on similar going is compelling, and Tom Clover's 5/20 T14 rate shows steady recent form.|

runners_data.name: Be Patient
runners_data.note: Strong form figures of 31-12 from Edward Bethell's yard and a genuine liking for good ground are the headline credentials; naturally wants to race prominently but is mapped to midfield because the prominent slots are already taken, which tempers the confidence in a winning shape that requires him to hold his natural berth.|

runners_data.name: First Officer
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's seven-year-old has a consistent placed record at 12f on good and similar surfaces but, like Be Patient, cannot secure his preferred prominent spot in this field configuration; his style fit score of 0.94 reflects that racing from further back than usual dilutes his chance meaningfully.|

races.paceDynamic: Round The Table is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just six runners over 1m4f at Newmarket's July course on good-to-firm ground, Jack Mitchell can dictate a controlled, measured tempo from the front without any genuine challenger for the lead. Tycoon and Race To The Stars are the natural prominent types who will track closely, likely settling just off Round The Table's shoulder, creating an organised, single-file procession rather than a contested early pace. Be Patient and First Officer are genuine prominent types by nature but, with the prominent berths already occupied, Jamie Spencer and Sorin Moldoveanu will find themselves deeper than ideal, leaving Astro King as the truest hold-up horse rearward. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop on fast ground over a staying trip — strongly favours horses who can race prominently in a settled rhythm or a well-timed front-runner who controls tempo, rather than true closers who need a genuine gallop to close into. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Round The Table and Tycoon are best placed to actually claim the positions they want, with Be Patient and First Officer most likely pushed wider and deeper than suits them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Round The Table dictates an uncontested, gallop and has enough in reserve to repel challengers from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Round The Table controls every yard of the race, setting a pace perfectly calibrated to suit his own stamina at 1m4f on fast ground, with no rival willing or able to press him.
winners: Tycoon and Race To The Stars
are best placed to mount a challenge but face the task of overhauling a horse that has never been put under early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Round The Table's gallop proves just too slow to stretch the field and Tycoon or Race To The Stars quicken past him approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A modest pace collapses the field into a bunch, turning the race into a sprint finish from the two-furlong marker, where Tycoon's course-and-distance form and Race To The Stars' class give them an edge.
winners: Both horses have been racing prominently throughout
so they avoid traffic problems and are positioned perfectly to use a late turn of foot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If Round The Table's pace is genuinely strong enough to soften up the prominent trio and Astro King finishes powerfully through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected tempo drains the leaders in the final quarter-mile, opening a gap on the rail for Astro King to thread through under Ebrahim Nader.
winners: Astro King's form shows finishing runs from the back and good-to-firm ground suits
but he needs more pace than this field is likely to generate
making this the least straightforward path.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Settled Order
scenarios.trigger: If a pace collapse or interference in the straight reshuffles the field and allows a redistributed hold-up type to steal it.
scenarios.body: Be Patient or First Officer, unable to settle in their preferred prominent position, find themselves with an unexpected run of daylight in the straight if the race bunches late.
winners: Their natural instinct to race forward could paradoxically help them if the leaders check or slow sharply
though their out-of-role position throughout remains a significant handicap.

watchPoints.text: Round The Table — if Jack Mitchell is allowed to control the gallop unchallenged from the off, monitor whether he is asked to pick up early in the straight or is given a flat-out sprint; the former scenario is harder for the field to peg back.

Be Patient and First Officer — watch the early stalls break to see whether either prominent type can slot closer than their mapped position; if they do get handy, their style fit improves sharply and the scenario probabilities shift.

Race To The Stars — 266 days off the track means fitness is unproven; if Appleby has him cherry-ripe the absence is irrelevant, but a below-par performance would quickly expose how much the race shape relies on the front two.

Astro King — watch whether any pace pressure materialises in the middle mile; this is the one factor that could bring him into contention, and without it Ebrahim Nader will have a near-impossible task making up ground on a controlled front-runner.

races.name: Racing Tv Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: In-form three-year-old with two wins at 7f on Good ground in his last five starts; Daniel Muscutt and James Fanshawe have an active 14-day record, prominent style suits this uncontested pace scenario perfectly, and OR 82 tops the field.

runners_data.name: Cancan In The Rain
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran carrying a headgear flag (p) and dropping to a more competitive OR; Gihan Arnolda's 14-day win rate is modest, but this horse's prominent style fits the tactical shape well despite a patchy record on similar going.

runners_data.name: Sunny Smile
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up filly fitted with hood and tongue-tie; Hugo Palmer has one winner from 24 in 14 days which is a quiet spell, and she has placed at 7f on Good twice — needs a gap to appear at the right moment.

runners_data.name: Here I Bow
runners_data.note: A genuine closer by nature who is mapped closer to the pace than he would prefer because there are too many hold-up types for the rear of the field to absorb; form figures are uninspiring (no wins or places on Good), and racing out of role diminishes his chance further.

runners_data.name: Piscean Star
runners_data.note: Promising three-year-old who won at 7f at Southwell and placed at the same trip; Mason Paetel claims five pounds which is valuable, Ed Dunlop has one winner from 17 runners in the past 14 days — prominent style is a natural fit here.

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for William Stone; eight years old and on a losing run of six but has placed three times on similar going and can control tempo entirely on his own terms — the key tactical fulcrum of the whole race.

runners_data.name: Sun Of Dolly
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose finishing position in the map understates how far back he would ideally race; Harry Vigors claims five pounds but this OR 60 three-year-old has no wins from seven starts on Good ground, and racing closer to the pace than ideal compounds the task.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' consistent four-year-old has placed six times in her last seven starts at 7f on Good, including two wins, and her raw form makes her the most dangerous closer in the field; that said, her true hold-up style is compressed into a tighter midfield position here, and Chloe Lyons' seven-pound claim is a useful offset.

runners_data.name: Where's Freddy
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer on board is noteworthy — the master of waiting tactics — but Where's Freddy's redistribution away from the rear means Spencer's hold-up game is constrained; one win at 7f on Good in the last five runs and fitted with hood and tongue-tie, so worth monitoring if a late gap emerges.

runners_data.name: Paladin
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell partners this five-year-old who won at 8f on Good last time and has two wins on similar ground; the step back to 7f may not be ideal, but the horse's hold-up style and Kevin & Lauren Frost's recent 14-day form (one from ten) suggest a place rather than a win is the ceiling here.

races.paceDynamic: Dashing Dick is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals pressing for the lead on the outside, he should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop down the Newmarket July Course straight seven. The going is Good to Firm, which will keep the pace honest without punishing the leader, and at OR 68 he is lightly weighted in absolute terms — meaning he can dictate tempo on his own terms without burning out. Prominent types Mr Writer, Cancan In The Rain and Piscean Star will sit just off the leader and are best placed to pounce if Dashing Dick stops, making this race shape a clear advantage for horses who can travel prominently and produce a short, sharp burst in the final two furlongs. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Here I Bow, Cherry Cobbler and Sun Of Dolly are genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, diluting their natural finishing kick. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: with a single pace-setter setting a sustainable tempo and no pressure to burn it up, horses racing prominently from positions two to four are best served, and true closers face an uphill task unless the pace collapses late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dashing Dick leads at a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent trio press him from two to four lengths off the pace.
scenarios.body: Dashing Dick sets a controlled tempo into the dip and the prominent challengers Mr Writer, Cancan In The Rain and Piscean Star quicken past him inside the final furlong on the fast ground; this shape strongly rewards horses who can travel sweetly close to the pace and produce a clean turn of foot on Good to Firm turf.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Dashing Dick steals an unassailable lead, forcing chasers to over-extend early.
scenarios.body: Dashing Dick bowls along unchallenged, the pace so moderate that prominent horses burn too much energy closing the gap in the final quarter mile; at the trip and on fast ground an eight-year-old front-runner who has shown course form can prove surprisingly hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Burst Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs or a significant gap opens up, allowing closers to find clear daylight.
scenarios.body: Cherry Cobbler, despite being pushed closer than ideal, has the highest raw form figures and consistent second-place finishes at this trip; if the prominent runners tie each other up, she and Where's Freddy — both genuine hold-up types — could emerge with a late rattle, though their redistributed positioning makes this shape less probable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If there is early crowding, a slow early pace creates a bunched field and the race is decided by a single surge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A compressed field on fast ground with no gaps can produce a random winner from the middle of the pack, with Sunny Smile and Paladin the most credible midfield beneficiaries given their going profiles; this is the least likely shape given Dashing Dick's presence to set an even tempo.

watchPoints.text: Dashing Dick controls the race tempo entirely alone — if Rob Hornby elects to go very slow through the early stages, the entire field is vulnerable to being outfoxed, and no one will be in a position to chase early without burning energy.

Cherry Cobbler has the strongest recent form profile in the race (five places including two wins in six starts at this trip on Good) but Stuart Williams runs two horses and Chloe Lyons' inexperience on a tactical track like Newmarket's July Course could cost her the ideal moment to challenge.

Here I Bow, Sun Of Dolly and Cherry Cobbler are all genuine hold-up types forced to race off the pace rather than from the back — monitor in-running positions; if all three find themselves closer than usual, the rear of the field may be unusually empty and any horse that does manage to get away will have no cover.

Jamie Spencer on Where's Freddy is worth tracking; Spencer routinely finds late gaps that others miss, and if the prominent runners cook each other in the final furlong, he is the most likely jockey to capitalise on a compressed finishing straight.

Piscean Star's apprentice Mason Paetel (5lb claim) races off a flat OR 76 at a track where pace-pressed three-year-olds can thrive on fast ground — watch whether he can slot in second or third behind Dashing Dick without being shuffled back.

races.name: Racing Welfare Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sibling Rivelry
runners_data.note: David Simcock's 4yo holds a career win over 12f on Good and races prominently; Taryn Langley's 3lb claim is useful on 139lbs and the 20-day turnaround is straightforward, though her recent form shows inconsistency at this sort of level.

runners_data.name: Expressionless
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who needs a genuine pace to exploit; Kyle McHugh's 5lb claim helps on 137lbs and the horse has placed 3/14f on Good before, but a lone, slow-burning front-runner is a difficult scenario for a horse with one win from 15 on similar ground.

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Most compelling distance profile in the field — back-to-back 14f placings and a 13f win, all on Good; Charlie Clover's stable is 3/9 in the last fortnight, the 12-day turnaround suggests freshness, and the prominent style allows him to shadow Society Girl throughout.

runners_data.name: Traveling Man
runners_data.note: Youngest in the field at three and lightest on the weights at 130lbs; the hold-up style suits a strongly-run race this distance, yet his sim-going record is only 3/4 and all four runs have come at 10-12f — the step to 14f on Good to Firm is an untested combination.

runners_data.name: Society Girl
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and race-shape controller; Ed Walker's 4/41 T14 is modest but she won over 12f on Good and handles this trip, and with zero rivals to press her, her ability to get away cheaply is a major tactical asset at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Society Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and will stride to the lead unchallenged from the outset, dictating a controlled, honest gallop over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. Sibling Rivelry and Jack Langley will look to race prominently just off her heels, meaning Society Girl faces no rival willing to burn her early, creating a sustainable, rhythm-based pace rather than a genuinely strong gallop. Expressionless and Traveling Man will be held up in the rear, needing either a step-up in tempo or a decisive Society Girl fade to deliver their finishing efforts into play. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track the leader at close quarters and pounce from a position of tactical advantage — the hold-up horses face a stern task if Society Girl controls the fractions and conserves enough to quicken late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Society Girl Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Society Girl dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and her rivals fail to apply meaningful pressure at any stage.
scenarios.body: Society Girl, unchallenged in front on Good to Firm ground she handles (4/6 sim-going), sets her own rhythm and proves impossible to reel in over 1m4f as the hold-up horses find too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Sibling Rivelry or Jack Langley track Society Girl seamlessly and produce a stronger turn-of-foot in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Both prominent types have the fitness and distance form to sit a length or two off the pace and capitalise if Society Girl ties up late; Jack Langley's recent course-and-distance wins (2 placings at 14f GOO) make him a natural beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Society Girl sets a faster-than-expected gallop that causes prominent runners to chase hard early, opening a gap for late finishers.
scenarios.body: Expressionless or Traveling Man could sweep through if the race develops into something more truly run, though both need the pace to genuinely stack up — Expressionless has only one win from 15 tries on similar going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Society Girl is taken on unexpectedly or loses her action and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the front.
scenarios.body: With no genuine challenger to the lead established, this is a low-probability event, but in such a scenario the freshest prominent horse or a luckily-placed hold-up runner scrambles home in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Society Girl — if she is allowed to bowl along at her own tempo unchallenged through the early furlongs, her front-running advantage becomes very hard for the hold-up pair to overcome over 1m4f.
Jack Langley — watch his position at the start; if he settles smoothly onto Society Girl's quarters within the first furlong, his course-and-distance form makes him the most dangerous shadow striker.
Traveling Man — his 3yo inexperience at this trip and over this trip on quick ground could see him outpaced in the middle stages if the apprentice jockey misjudges the pace from the rear.

Expressionless — headgear (p) noted; watch whether the headgear produces a more positive early move, as his usual hold-up role is ill-suited to a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo by a lone leader.
